prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Charlotte for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist for implants — the right provider depends on your specific needs (surgical complexity, bone grafting, full-arch vs single-tooth, budget, comfort with sedation, etc.). That said, for predictable implant outcomes you should look for a specialist with strong implant experience and the right credentials.

How to find the best implant provider in Charlotte
- Prefer a specialist for surgery and/or restoration:
  - Oral & maxillofacial surgeons (OMS) — for complex surgery, IV sedation, bone grafts, extractions.
  - Periodontists — experts in the gums and bone; many place implants.
  - Prosthodontists — specialists in implant restorations (crowns, bridges, full-arch prostheses).
  - Some general dentists with extensive implant training also do excellent work for straightforward cases.
- Look for these credentials and experience:
  - Board certification (ABOMS for oral surgeons, American Board of Periodontology board certification, or American Board of Prosthodontics for prosthodontists) or fellowship/advance training in implants.
  - Years of experience and number of implants placed annually.
  - Use of modern diagnostics (CBCT/3D imaging) and guided implant planning.
  - Good before/after photos and patient references.
  - Clear warranty/maintenance plan and communication about costs and timeline.
- Ask these questions at a consult:
  - Who will do the surgery and who will do the restoration?
  - Do you use CBCT for planning and do you offer guided surgery?
  - How many implants do you place per year? What is your complication rate?
  - Do you perform bone grafts/sinus lifts if needed?
  - What implant systems do you use and why?
  - What anesthesia/sedation options are offered?
  - Can I see before/after photos and patient testimonials?
- Where to look for vetted providers:
  - AAOMS “Find a Surgeon” (oral surgeons), American Academy of Periodontology “Find a Periodontist,” American College of Prosthodontists “Find a Prosthodontist,” and the American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID) listings.
  - Local review sites: Google Reviews, Healthgrades, Zocdoc, Yelp — watch for consistent themes (care, follow-up, outcomes).
  - Ask your general dentist for their recommended implant surgeons/restorative partners.

If you want, I can:
- Look up and list top-rated implant specialists in Charlotte (I’ll need your zip code or area and whether you prefer oral surgery, periodontist, or prosthodontist), or
- Help you draft a list of questions to bring to consultations.

Which would you like?
